newsitem.title: MADAGASCAR: Two former presidents in Madagascar run-off poll.
newsitem.headline: Two former presidents in Madagascar run-off poll.

text.p: Madagascar's former military leader Didier Ratsiraka and former president Albert Zafy will contest a second round of presidential elections in the new year.
Official results announced on Monday of the first round of voting on November 3 showed Ratsiraka took 36.61 percent against 23.39 percent for Zafy.
Boto Victor, president of the High Constitutional Court (HCC), reported numerous anomalies in the first round of voting but said they did not change the overall results.
The election was called after Zafy, 69, who was elected president in 1993, was impeached by parliament in July for abuse of his authority. The HCC upheld the impeachment.

The strength of support for Ratsiraka, a 59-year-old retired admiral, has surprised many observers. He was reviled by many of his people in the early 1990s for using the army to resist the pro-democracy movement on the vast island with a population of 14 million, most of whom live in chronic poverty.
Victor noted that according to the constitution the second round run-off should take place within 31 days of the results.

But interim president Norbert Ratsirahonana told reporters that the second round would probably take place after 31 days because of the New Year holidays and the need for the costs of the second round to be part of the 1997 budget.
"This is why the government is going to ask the High Constitutional Court to authorise an exceptional delay because on this issue it has the last word," Ratsirahonana said.

The HCC said millionaire businessman Herizo Razafimahaleo took 15.13 percent of the first round vote followed by Ratsirahonana with 10.14 percent. Parliament Speaker Richard Andriamanjato took 4.94 percent. Ten other candidates took between two and 0.37 percent.
